fr.recommendations:
• Mark the single access road entrance with a clearly visible address sign readable from both directions of approach.

• Post the address or property identifier at the access road entry point, not only at the main building, to allow responding units to confirm they have reached the correct property before reaching the structures.

• Mark the secondary building with its own visible identifier to allow responding units to distinguish it from the main building during an incident.

• Keep the access road clear of parked vehicles or stored equipment along its length, as it is the only vehicle entry and exit point for the property.

• Identify and mark a designated staging area for emergency vehicles that does not block the single access road.

• Keep the outdoor storage area organized so that stored materials do not restrict movement around the buildings or block access for responding units.

• Mark any walking paths or ground-level routes between the main building and secondary building to allow responders to move between structures without navigating through dense vegetation.

• Trim vegetation along the access road to maintain clear sightlines and overhead clearance for emergency vehicles.

• Confirm that the area around the retention pond is clearly distinguishable at night or in low-visibility conditions to prevent responders from approaching its edge unknowingly.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim trees and shrubs that are growing directly against or overhanging any buildings in the cluster.
• Remove vegetation growing in contact with building walls, foundations, or overhangs.
• Thin shrubs and mixed vegetation concentrated immediately around the building cluster to create open separation between plants and structures.
• Keep the area between tree clusters and buildings as open as possible by removing low branches and shrubs that connect ground-level vegetation to tree canopies.
• Maintain the open green spaces between vegetation and buildings — avoid planting or allowing vegetation to fill these gaps.
• Clear any dead or dry plant material from around building entrances, walkways, and walls.
• Verify that firefighters can move completely around all buildings in the cluster — remove any vegetation, debris, or stored materials blocking passage along building perimeters.
• Improve rear access by clearing vegetation, debris, or other obstacles that restrict movement behind the buildings.
• Keep drive lanes and access roads free of encroaching vegetation from both sides.
• Mark or keep clear any access points that provide entry to the rear of the property so responders can locate them quickly.
